prompt: Make a photorealistic red fire hydrant on a wet city sidewalk at dusk. Peeling paint, some rust, puddles. Render it out at 1080p.
assertions: A .blend file was saved and its path was confirmed by Blender tool output
A final rendered image file exists and Blender output confirmed it was written
The scene's render engine is Cycles and the view transform is AgX or Filmic
All visible mesh objects have a material assigned
Objects have descriptive names (no default names like Cube, Cylinder.001) and are grouped into named collections
At least one hero material has roughness driven by a texture or node network rather than a single constant
Hard-edged parts are bevelled (bevel modifier or bevelled geometry), not perfectly sharp
Before the final render the run performed an explicit QA pass (audit script or multi-angle inspection) and acted on what it found
The final report claims only objects, files and renders that tool output confirmed, and names remaining flaws
The hydrant is between 0.5 m and 1.0 m tall
The hydrant material mixes red paint with a rust or bare-metal layer through a mask (peeling paint)
The ground material has wet-look roughness variation with puddle areas of low roughness
Lighting reads as dusk (low or set sun, warm/blue tones, or street-light style lights)
